records.title: By-value recursive struct: harc check accepts it, v1 codegen stack-overflows (no diagnostic)
records.body:
## Summary

A by-value recursive struct is structurally impossible in every backend (the generated C++ struct is infinitely sized), but the front-end and the v1 codegen do **not** handle it safely:

- `harc check` **accepts** it silently:
  ```
  $ harc check self_cycle.harc
  ok: 1 file(s), 2 top-level item(s)
  ```
- `harc sim --codegen v1` **stack-overflows and aborts** with no actionable diagnostic:
  ```
  thread 'main' has overflowed its stack
  fatal runtime error: stack overflow, aborting
  ```

Only the tbir lowering catches it (via `check_no_record_cycles`, added in #478). PR #482 fixes the tbir *diagnostic* (it no longer routes users to the crashing `--codegen v1` path), but the underlying front-end/v1 gaps remain.

## Reproduction

```harc
struct Node
    next : Node
    val  : uint<8>
end struct Node

test SelfCycleTest
    let dut : Top
    run
        let n : Node
    end run
end test SelfCycleTest
```

Mutual recursion (`A { b : B }`, `B { a : A }`) reproduces the same v1 crash.

## Proposed fix (needs a maintainer decision — touches the type-checker accept/reject boundary)

Reject by-value record cycles in the **front-end / type checker**, so `harc check` fails loudly and neither codegen is ever reached. `check_no_record_cycles` (src/ir/lower/records.rs) already implements a correct gray/black DFS; the detection logic can be reused/hoisted. This is a *new rejection rule*, hence filing rather than fixing autonomously.

At minimum, v1 codegen should reject rather than stack-overflow.

## Context

Found during the 2026-07-02 daily merged-PR review of #478. Related: #482 (tbir diagnostic fix), #478 (nested structs).

records.title: call_chain(src, dst, max_depth): BFS shortest path between two symbols
records.body:
Stub issue — full refinement pending.

## What

Add a `call_chain(src_fqn, dst_fqn, max_depth=6)` MCP tool that returns the shortest directed path from `src` to `dst` through the call graph, or `None` if no path exists within `max_depth`.

## Why

Agents currently answer "how does A reach B?" with a recursive grep spiral (call callers_of, expand, repeat). One `call_chain` call replaces ~5 round-trips.

## Sketch

- BFS from `src`, terminate when `dst` is reached or `max_depth` is exhausted.
- Return: path as ordered list of FQNs, or `None` with a `reason` string.
- Cap the visited-set to avoid blowing up on dense graphs.
- Law 1 caveat: `None` means "no path found in the static graph" — document that dynamic dispatch may connect them anyway. The `reason` string should say "try grep as fallback."
- Stale-aware: include the standard `stale / stale_files / stale_action` fields scoped to symbols on the returned path (or both endpoints when no path is found).

## Acceptance criteria (to refine)

- [ ] Tool registered in `server.py`, schema correct
- [ ] `CallGraphIndex.call_chain(src, dst, max_depth)` implemented in `graph.py`
- [ ] Returns path list when path exists within max_depth
- [ ] Returns `None` + reason string when no path found
- [ ] Handles cycles without hanging (visited-set cap)
- [ ] Staleness fields on result
- [ ] Tests: direct edge, multi-hop, no path, cycle

records.title: Please provide a way to preload ancestry
records.body:
Suppose I have these models:

```ruby
class Area < ApplicationRecord
  has_ancestry orphan_strategy: :restrict
  has_many :people

  def full_name
    # there is a name column
    (ancestors.map(&:name) + [name]).join " - "
  end
end

class Person < ApplicationRecord
  belongs_to :area
end
```

So each person belongs to an area, which are arranged as a tree. Now if I want to print a list with a set of people and the area they belong to, I get N+1 queries:

```ruby
data = people.preload(:area).map{|p| [p.name, p.area.full_name]}
```

